basis: Worth nil: generic ticagrelor has been sold in the US since 2025-05-01 (FDA Paragraph IV list for NDA 22433, first marketing 2025-05-01; openFDA Drugs@FDA ANDAs 208584 Apotex 2025-05-01, 208576 Alembic 2025-05-02, 208537 InvaGen 2025-05-05, all marketed, queried 2026-11-16) and AstraZeneca reports Brilinta US revenue of $16m for the nine months to 2026-09-30, down 95%, 'Decline driven by generic entry in the US and Europe in Q2 2025' (6-K 0001654954-26-009256, filed 2026-10-30). The only Orange Book patent left, 10300065 to 2036, carries use codes U-2541 and U-2542 (60 mg after MI or ACS), so nothing protects a stroke use. CAPTIVA is academic, not AstraZeneca's: sponsor University of Florida, NINDS grant U01NS117450, AstraZeneca and Janssen collaborators, 1,683 US patients across 114 US sites, ticagrelor plus aspirin and rivaroxaban plus aspirin each against clopidogrel plus aspirin, primary completion 2027-01-31 (registry, checked 2026-11-16). The label already covers part of the population, 'to reduce the risk of stroke in patients with acute ischemic stroke (NIH Stroke Scale score <=5) or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA)' (DailyMed setid f7b3f443-e83d-4bf2-0e96-023448fed9a8, SPL 56). Draft pos 0.0 row in nil_rows.csv moves the readout to programme_stopped with this source

Worth nil, though the gap is real. The label excludes the population: 'Initiation with FARXIGA is not recommended in patients with an eGFR less than 25 mL/min/1.73 m2' (openFDA set 72ad22ae-efe6-4cd6-a302-98aaee423d69, version 49, effective 2026-06-03). But generic dapagliflozin was approved and launched on 2026-04-06 (openFDA Drugs@FDA ANDAs 211312 Sandoz, 211478 MSN, 211468 Aurobindo, 211470 Biocon, all marketed; FDA Paragraph IV list for NDA 202293, first marketing 2026-04-06, queried 2026-11-16), and AstraZeneca reports Farxiga US revenue of $795m for the nine months to 2026-09-30, down 36%, 'Multiple generics launched in Q2 2026' (6-K 0001654954-26-009256, filed 2026-10-30). RENAL LIFECYCLE reads out 2027-07, fifteen months after generic entry, is sponsored by University Medical Center Groningen (AstraZeneca and the Dutch Kidney Foundation collaborate) and has no US site: Australia, Belgium, Germany, the Netherlands, Singapore and Spain only, 1,750 patients, dapagliflozin 10 mg against placebo (registry, checked 2026-11-16). Draft pos 0.0 row in nil_rows.csv

SURMOUNT-MMO is an outcomes study inside the approved population, the Zepbound analogue of SELECT. Label: 'ZEPBOUND is indicated in combination with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity: to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in adults with obesity or adults with overweight in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition' (DailyMed setid 487cd7e7-434c-4925-99fa-aa80b1cc776b, SPL 40, openFDA effective 2026-08-28). Trial: BMI 27.0 or more, age 40 or more with established cardiovascular disease, or older adults with cardiovascular risk factors, diabetes excluded, 15,374 enrolled, primary outcome time to death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, coronary revascularisation or heart failure event, primary completion 2027-10 (registry, checked 2026-11-16). A win adds a claim, not patients. The book already says so: lly_zepbound.csv carries Obesity base_pool_overlap_pct 1.0. THE ROW READS needs_layer ONLY BECAUSE OF A LINK DEFECT: catalyst 798 carries asset_indication_id 118, which is Mounjaro (asset 126) and Obesity, not Zepbound's own pair 133 (asset 138, indication 15). indication_layer.build is called on Mounjaro, which has no Obesity assumptions. Relinking catalyst 798 to pair 133 should make it already_approved or in_the_base; no seed row is needed

Oral Wegovy is approved: NDA 218316 (Wegovy tablets 1.5, 4, 9 and 25 mg), original approval 2025-12-22, five labelling supplements since (openFDA Drugs@FDA, queried 2026-11-16). Label: 'WEGOVY tablets are indicated in combination with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity: ... to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in adults with obesity, or in adults with overweight in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition' (DailyMed setid ee06186f-2aa3-4990-a760-757579d8f77b, SPL 19, 2026-06-30). OASIS 5 enrols adults with BMI 30.0 or more, or 27.0 or more with at least one weight-related comorbidity, HbA1c below 6.5%, two oral doses against placebo, primary outcome relative change in body weight at week 60, 450 patients, primary completion 2028-02-22 (registry, checked 2026-11-16): the label's population word for word. nvo_wegovy.csv already carries Obesity base_pool_overlap_pct 1.0. SAME LINK DEFECT AS ZEPBOUND: catalyst 1106 carries asset_indication_id 121, which is Ozempic (asset 128) and Obesity, and Wegovy (asset 136) has no Obesity pair in asset_indications at all; the fix is a Wegovy/Obesity pair and a relink, not a seed row

A postmarketing safety and dosing requirement, not an expansion. NCT06568939 is AbbVie study M25-274 (registry org study id), which FDA imposed at approval as PMR 4844-2 under section 505(o): 'Complete clinical trial, Study M25-274 ... to further assess known serious risks with telisotuzumab vedotin including interstitial lung disease, ocular disorders, and other severe adverse reactions, evaluating alternative dosages (flat dosage 1.9 mg/kg Q2W vs flat dosage 1.6 mg/kg Q2W vs. 1.6 mg/kg -> 1.9 mg/kg Q2W dose up-titration)' (BLA 761384 approval letter, 2025-05-14, Reference ID 5590638, accessdata.fda.gov). Primary outcomes are adverse event rates (any grade, ILD, neuropathy, ocular, discontinuation, grade 5) plus ORR, three telisotuzumab arms, no comparator, 150 patients, primary completion 2028-02 (registry, checked 2026-11-16). It admits c-Met 25% or more 3+, wider than the label's 'high c-Met protein overexpression [>=50% of tumor cells with strong (3+) staining] ... who have received a prior systemic therapy' (DailyMed setid bc04f980-3957-4e35-ab81-8ec2ffe87215), but the study that verifies benefit and could widen the claim is M18-868, NCT04928846, PMR 4844-1, primary completion 2028-12. Price and discontinuation are therefore not pursued for this readout

A master protocol of two molecules and two diseases, not one readout. Subprotocol A is inebilizumab (3 or 4 doses) in biopsy-proven class III or IV lupus nephritis with inadequate response to at least one therapy; subprotocols B and C are blinatumomab (Blincyto) in SLE and refractory rheumatoid arthritis. Primary outcomes for subprotocol A are treatment-emergent and serious treatment-emergent adverse events to week 52; the efficacy primaries (complete renal response, DORIS remission, DAS28-CRP remission) belong to blinatumomab cohorts. Phase 2, open label, non-randomised, 220 patients across the protocol, 'Subprotocol A and B are no longer recruiting', and the 2028-08-06 primary completion is the whole platform's (registry, checked 2026-11-16). Amgen: 'A Phase 2 study of inebilizumab in autoimmune disease has completed enrollment of adults with SLE with nephritis' (Q3 2026 results, 8-K 0000318154-26-000153, 2026-11-03). Label: NMOSD (AQP4 positive), IgG4-related disease and generalised myasthenia gravis in adults (openFDA set 834db232-afb0-4dcf-93e0-009ce8245c20, version 11, 2026-09-21). The inebilizumab arm is an uncontrolled safety readout in nephritis, a narrower disease than the book's SLE pool, so the ASP price was not pursued

SHASTA-10 is 'A Phase 3 Open-Label Extension Study to Evaluate the Long-Term Safety and Efficacy of Plozasiran in Adults With Hypertriglyceridemia': single group, no masking, entry requires having 'Completed all required study visits per protocol in the parent study', primary outcome number of participants with treatment-emergent adverse events to month 24, 710 enrolled, primary completion 2028-07 (registry, sponsor study AROAPOC3-3006, checked 2026-11-16). The sHTG value rides on the parent studies, all completed: SHASTA-3 NCT06347003 (pcd 2026-06-12), SHASTA-4 NCT06347016 (2026-06-17) and MUIR-3 NCT06347133 (2026-06-01). Arrowhead 'has submitted a Supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) to the U.S. FDA and is currently preparing for a potential U.S. launch in sHTG in the second quarter of 2027', and 'In October 2026, the FDA granted entry into the STAR pilot program for the Company's sNDA for plozasiran for the treatment of sHTG' (FY2026 10-K 0000879407-26-000078, filed 2026-11-12). Label today: 'adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS)' (DailyMed setid 7fd37993-f85a-4af1-8bbe-133299f226ed, SPL 4). The gate is the sNDA decision, which the book has no catalyst for

A real but small expansion that cannot be priced from free sources. Outside the label: 'POMBILITI is indicated, in combination with Opfolda, for the treatment of adult patients with late-onset Pompe disease ... weighing >=40 kg and who are not improving on their current enzyme replacement therapy (ERT)' (DailyMed setid d77aa596-910d-516b-e053-2995a90a0839, SPL 8, 2026-08-17); ROSSELLA (ATB200-08) enrols IOPD aged 0 to under 18, 36 patients, open label, primary outcome infusion-associated reactions at 104 weeks, primary completion 2027-07 (registry, checked 2026-11-16). Sourced: US IOPD incidence 23 a year, 63 cases in 9,794,141 US newborns screened, 1 in 155,463 (Colburn and Lapidus, Front Pediatr 2024;11:1221140, PMID 38274468, PMC10810242) on 3,628,934 2024 births (NVSR 75-02); overlap 0.0; default ramp. Refused: prevalence (no free US survival of treated IOPD to 18), eligible_pct, penetration_peak_pct, discontinuation_pct, and net_price_per_patient (CMS 2024 holds 13 adult beneficiaries in each of Part B and Part D, and a 20 mg/kg drug cannot be priced for children without an age and weight mix). Partial draft in bmrn_pombiliti_rows.csv. Owner now correct: BioMarin completed the Amicus merger on 2026-04-27 (Amicus 8-K 0001140361-26-016968, Item 2.01)

A real expansion with a free pool and no free price. Outside the label: 'PALSONIFY is indicated for the treatment of adults with acromegaly who had an inadequate response to surgery and/or for whom surgery is not an option' (openFDA set 8a6d2ce0-a621-4ee7-983c-977cd948ff4d, version 3). CAREFNDR is a randomised, quadruple-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 of paltusotine 80 mg daily in carcinoid syndrome due to well-differentiated NETs, primary outcome flushing frequency at week 12, 141 patients, primary completion 2027-08 (registry, sponsor study CRN00808-12, checked 2026-11-16). Sourced: prevalence 32,168, the 171,321 US NET 20-year prevalence of 2014 (Dasari, JAMA Oncol 2017, PMID 28448665) times the 1,786 of 9,512 NETs with carcinoid syndrome at diagnosis (Halperin, Lancet Oncol 2017, PMID 28238592); incidence 4,457, 6.98 per 100,000 on 340,110,988 (Census V2024) times the same share; overlap 0.0; default ramp. Refused: net_price_per_patient (Crinetics sells at an unpublished WAC, reports no patients on drug, and Medicaid SDUD suppresses every national Palsonify row for 2025 Q4 and 2026 Q1), discontinuation_pct, eligible_pct, penetration_peak_pct. Partial draft in vrtx_palsonify_rows.csv. Owner now correct: Vertex completed the Crinetics merger on 2026-09-01 (Crinetics 8-K 0001140361-26-035195, Item 2.01; Form 15 2026-09-11)
